Battle of the Hills.fact: Few German defences remained intact, except for those in Bois de la Grille and around Aubérive. In the west, from Bois de la Grille to Tranchée du Bois du Chien, the bombardment.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: South of _____, the Konstanzlager and the row of dugouts up the south slope of Mont Perthois, had not been seriously damaged
Battle of the Hills.fact: South of Mont Haut, the Konstanzlager and the row of dugouts up the south slope of Mont Perthois, had not been seriously damaged. Most of the German defences on the southern slopes of Mont Cornillet, Mont Blond, Mont Haut and Mont Perthois had been badly damaged but many intermediate strong points, machine-gun nests remained.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The French Fourth Army offensive against the German _____th Army was to support the Groupe d'armées du Nord (GAN, Northern Army Group) along the Chemin des Dames, in the Second Battle of the Aisne
Battle of the Hills.fact: The French Fourth Army offensive against the German 4th Army was to support the Groupe d'armées du Nord (GAN, Northern Army Group) along the Chemin des Dames, in the Second Battle of the Aisne. On the left of XII Corps to the east of the Suippes river, the 24th Division set up a flank guard by attacking through Bois des Abattis towards Germains and Baden-Baden trenches.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: North-east of Mont Haut, the advance reached a depth of _____ (1.5 mi) and next day the advance was pressed further
Battle of the Hills.fact: North-east of Mont Haut, the advance reached a depth of 2.4 km (1.5 mi) and next day the advance was pressed further.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The Fourth Army held an _____ (11 mi) front, just north of the Reims, St Hilaire le Grand, St Ménéhould to Verdun road, between Massiges and Ferme Marquises, about 120 m (400 ft) below the peak of Mon
Battle of the Hills.fact: The Fourth Army held an 18 km (11 mi) front, just north of the Reims, St Hilaire le Grand, St Ménéhould to Verdun road, between Massiges and Ferme Marquises, about 120 m (400 ft) below the peak of Mont Haut.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: To reach the summit, the French infantry would have to advance about _____ (2 mi) up a series of steep rises
Battle of the Hills.fact: To reach the summit, the French infantry would have to advance about 3.2 km (2 mi) up a series of steep rises.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The French bombardment opened on _____ April, against the German first, second and third lines on the south side of the ridge
Battle of the Hills.fact: The French bombardment opened on 10 April, against the German first, second and third lines on the south side of the ridge.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Most of the _____ defences on the southern slopes of Mont Cornillet, Mont Blond, Mont Haut and Mont Perthois had been badly damaged but many intermediate strong points, machine-gun nests remained
Battle of the Hills.fact: The second line, half-way up the slopes of the Moronvilliers hills, was destroyed from south of Mont Perthois to the Suippes, barbed-wire in the woods to the north-east of Mont Sans Nom was partially cut, making an attack on the German position on the ridges above the Suippes practicable. In the west, from Bois de la Grille to Tranchée du Bois du Chien, the bombardment was less effective and the German defences in Bois de la Grille and Leopoldshöhe Trench behind it and Erfurt Trench to the ea...

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Vaudesincourt was then to be captured and the right flank was to link with the centre, which was to take Côte 181 and _____
Battle of the Hills.fact: Vaudesincourt was then to be captured and the right flank was to link with the centre, which was to take Côte 181 and Mont Sans Nom.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: If Le Téton had not been captured, the troops in the French centre, were to drive the _____ from Bois de Côte 144 and attack the hill from the east
Battle of the Hills.fact: If Le Téton had not been captured, the troops in the French centre, were to drive the Germans from Bois de Côte 144 and attack the hill from the east.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: East of the _____, on the right flank of the XVII Corps, four and a half battalions were to attack Aubérive and the trenches beyond, up to those at the western fringe of Bois des Abatis
Battle of the Hills.fact: The fortified village of Vaudesincourt to the north, on the banks of the Suippes and the maze of trenches on the right bank, had been badly damaged but much of the wire was uncut and blockhouses and pill-boxes had not been destroyed. East of the Suippes, on the right flank of the XVII Corps, four and a half battalions were to attack Aubérive and the trenches beyond, up to those at the western fringe of Bois des Abatis.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Just in front of _____ was Mont Perthois, at about the same height as Mont Cornillet
Battle of the Hills.fact: On the right flank of the XVII Corps, one division was to capture Le Casque, its wood and Le Téton; on the left flank the divisional objectives were the summits of Mont Haut, Mont Perthois and the trenches linking Mont Haut to Le Casque. Just in front of Mont Haut was Mont Perthois, at about the same height as Mont Cornillet.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: An attack from the south on _____ and Mont Haut, could be subjected to enfilade fire by the Germans on Mont Cornillet and Mont Perthois
Battle of the Hills.fact: The VIII Corps (General Hely d'Oissel), was to capture Mont Cornillot and Mont Blond, Flensburg Trench and the next one behind, which connected the defences of the summits, Mont Blond, Mont Cornillot, Bois de la Grille and Leopoldshöhe Trench. An attack from the south on Mont Blond and Mont Haut, could be subjected to enfilade fire by the Germans on Mont Cornillet and Mont Perthois.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Mont Sans Nom lay about _____ (1.5 mi) to the south-east of Le Téton, at the same height as Mont Blond, with Côte 181 at the south end
Battle of the Hills.fact: Mont Sans Nom lay about 2.4 km (1.5 mi) to the south-east of Le Téton, at the same height as Mont Blond, with Côte 181 at the south end.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Two tunnels, capable of accommodating several battalions of infantry, had been dug under the north slope of _____ and the north-east side of Mont Perthois
Battle of the Hills.fact: Two tunnels, capable of accommodating several battalions of infantry, had been dug under the north slope of Mont Cornillet and the north-east side of Mont Perthois.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The German defences between the Suippes and the Vesle, lay on a plateau overlooked by Mont Berru _____ (876 ft) high and along Moronvilliers Ridge, which was about 10 km (6.2 mi) long and about 210 m
Battle of the Hills.fact: The German defences between the Suippes and the Vesle, lay on a plateau overlooked by Mont Berru 267 m (876 ft) high and along Moronvilliers Ridge, which was about 10 km (6.2 mi) long and about 210 m (690 ft) high.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The ridge dominated the plain of Châlons and there was a parallel, lower ridge about _____ (430 ft) high, which met the main ridge at the village of Beine; the two ridges declined steeply to the south
Battle of the Hills.fact: The ridge dominated the plain of Châlons and there was a parallel, lower ridge about 130 m (430 ft) high, which met the main ridge at the village of Beine; the two ridges declined steeply to the south.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: A fifth reserve position, the _____ lay further back
Battle of the Hills.fact: A fifth reserve position, the Suippesstellung lay further back.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: German possession of _____ and Mont Sans Nom meant that a French attack on Le Casque and Le Téton could be engaged by crossfire
Battle of the Hills.fact: German possession of Mont Perthois and Mont Sans Nom meant that a French attack on Le Casque and Le Téton could be engaged by crossfire.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The main _____ defensive position was in the ruins of Bois de la Grille to the south-west of Mont Cornillet and west of the Thuizy–Nauroy road
Battle of the Hills.fact: German possession of Mont Perthois and Mont Sans Nom meant that a French attack on Le Casque and Le Téton could be engaged by crossfire. The hills on the edge of the Châlons plain could be outflanked from west to east, only after the German defences on either side of the Thuizy–Nauroy road and between Mont Sans Nom and the Suippes had been captured.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: An attack from the east on the hills was blocked by the entrenchments from _____ to the Suippes, which ran south-east around Aubérive-sur-Suippes on the left bank of the river
Battle of the Hills.fact: German possession of Mont Perthois and Mont Sans Nom meant that a French attack on Le Casque and Le Téton could be engaged by crossfire. The hills on the edge of the Châlons plain could be outflanked from west to east, only after the German defences on either side of the Thuizy–Nauroy road and between Mont Sans Nom and the Suippes had been captured.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: North of Aubérive on the left bank was the fortified village of Vaudesincourt on the _____-l'Heureux road
Battle of the Hills.fact: North of Aubérive on the left bank was the fortified village of Vaudesincourt on the St Martin-l'Heureux road. Near the Suippes, a network of trenches followed the ridge above the river to St Martin-l'Heureux.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The Germans had dug several lines of trenches from north to south, on the west and east slopes of the hills, the trenches on the west running north and west of _____
Battle of the Hills.fact: The main German defensive position was in the ruins of Bois de la Grille to the south-west of Mont Cornillet and west of the Thuizy–Nauroy road. The Germans had dug several lines of trenches from north to south, on the west and east slopes of the hills, the trenches on the west running north and west of Nauroy.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: In front of _____ was another trench, which linked the defences on top of Mont Cornillet
Battle of the Hills.fact: The Germans had dug several lines of trenches from north to south, on the west and east slopes of the hills, the trenches on the west running north and west of Nauroy. In front of Nauroy was another trench, which linked the defences on top of Mont Cornillet.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Near the _____, a network of trenches followed the ridge above the river to St Martin-l'Heureux
Battle of the Hills.fact: Near the Suippes, a network of trenches followed the ridge above the river to St Martin-l'Heureux. An advance down the right bank of the Suippes, towards Dontrien and St Martin-l'Heureux and the Bazancourt to Somme-Py and Apremont railway, was obstructed by a trench system east of Aubérive and Bois de la Côte 152.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Higher up the slope, another trench led to _____ de la Côte 179 and protected Le Téton from an attack from the north-east
Battle of the Hills.fact: Higher up the slope, another trench led to Grand Bois de la Côte 179 and protected Le Téton from an attack from the north-east.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The first _____ line in the south of this defensive zone, comprised several parallel trenches connected by communication trenches, with numerous dug-outs, concrete blockhouses and pill-boxes
Battle of the Hills.fact: The first German line in the south of this defensive zone, comprised several parallel trenches connected by communication trenches, with numerous dug-outs, concrete blockhouses and pill-boxes.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: A second line higher up the ridge, was joined to the first by the _____öhe Trench, a fortified approach from the north of Bois de la Grille to the Thuizy–Nauroy road
Battle of the Hills.fact: A second line higher up the ridge, was joined to the first by the Leopoldshöhe Trench, a fortified approach from the north of Bois de la Grille to the Thuizy–Nauroy road. The Leopoldshöhe Trench was continued to the east, below the summits of Mont Cornillet, Mont Blond, Mont Haut and Mont Perthois, by Erfurt Trench.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: South of _____ and Le Téton, it became graben du Bois du Chien, Landtag Trench and then Landsturm Trench, to the positions on the east slope of the hills
Battle of the Hills.fact: South of Le Casque and Le Téton, it became graben du Bois du Chien, Landtag Trench and then Landsturm Trench, to the positions on the east slope of the hills.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The trench ran below and Côte 181 and _____
Battle of the Hills.fact: The trench ran below and Côte 181 and Mont Sans Nom.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Behind the _____ second line, the hilltops had been wired for all-round defence, connected by communication trenches
Battle of the Hills.fact: Behind the German second line, the hilltops had been wired for all-round defence, connected by communication trenches. Every move by the French, was under observation from the German positions but the ridge from Mont Cornillet to Le Téton and the woods to the west and east, hid German movements from ground observation and could only be detected by French aviators, who were frequently grounded by bad weather in the winter and spring of 1916–1917.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The crests of the hills had been fortified on the south and north sides; on the northern slope of _____ and the north-east side of Mont Perthois, were the defensive tunnels
Battle of the Hills.fact: The crests of the hills had been fortified on the south and north sides; on the northern slope of Mont Cornillet and the north-east side of Mont Perthois, were the defensive tunnels. The tunnel entrances were invisible to air observation and a French advance across the top of Mont Cornillet could be attacked from behind from them.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The tunnel entrances were invisible to air observation and a French advance across the top of _____ could be attacked from behind from them
Battle of the Hills.fact: The crests of the hills had been fortified on the south and north sides; on the northern slope of Mont Cornillet and the north-east side of Mont Perthois, were the defensive tunnels. The tunnel entrances were invisible to air observation and a French advance across the top of Mont Cornillet could be attacked from behind from them.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Generalleutnant (_____-General) Georg von Gersdorf, the 58th Division commander, disagreed with Beaulieu and eventually resigned
Battle of the Hills.fact: Generalleutnant (Lieutenant-General) Georg von Gersdorf, the 58th Division commander, disagreed with Beaulieu and eventually resigned.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The German defences were held by the 30th _____, 58th Division, 214th Division and 29th Division from east to west
Battle of the Hills.fact: During Easter, General Martin Chales de Beaulieu, the XIV Corps commander and the general commanding the 214th Division at Moronvilliers, briefed his subordinates that only artillery demonstrations were likely, between Reims and Aubérive. Generalleutnant (Lieutenant-General) Georg von Gersdorf, the 58th Division commander, disagreed with Beaulieu and eventually resigned.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The German artillery was reinforced from 150 four-gun batteries on 1 _____, to 200 to 250 batteries
Battle of the Hills.fact: On 10 April, the bombardment by the Fourth Army began, with such force that Beaulieu ordered the German garrisons to prepare for immediate attack and warned the reserve and Eingreifdivisionen (specialist counter-attack divisions), the 32nd Division from St Quentin, the 23rd Division from Sedan and the 5th Division and 6th Division in Alsace, to be ready to move to the Moronvilliers area; the 32nd Division began to move on 15 April. The German artillery was reinforced from 150 four-gun batteri...

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: With reinforcements, there were four divisions on the flanks and the _____ massif in between and four divisions in close reserve
Battle of the Hills.fact: On 10 April, the bombardment by the Fourth Army began, with such force that Beaulieu ordered the German garrisons to prepare for immediate attack and warned the reserve and Eingreifdivisionen (specialist counter-attack divisions), the 32nd Division from St Quentin, the 23rd Division from Sedan and the 5th Division and 6th Division in Alsace, to be ready to move to the Moronvilliers area; the 32nd Division began to move on 15 April. With reinforcements, there were four divisions on the flanks ...

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: It was still dark when the Fourth Army, on the left of Groupe d'armées de Centre (GAC, Central Army Group) attacked at 4.45 a.m., from Aubérive east of Reims, with the XII, XVII and VIII corps, on an
Battle of the Hills.fact: It was still dark when the Fourth Army, on the left of Groupe d'armées de Centre (GAC, Central Army Group) attacked at 4.45 a.m., from Aubérive east of Reims, with the XII, XVII and VIII corps, on an 11 km (6.8 mi) front.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The 24th _____ with 4+1⁄2 battalions, attacked on a line from the salient at Bois des Abatis, west to the Suippes, north of Bois des Sapins
Battle of the Hills.fact: In the XII Corps area on the right flank, the 24th Division, Moroccan Division and the 75th Territorial Regiment of XVII Corps, were to attack from the east bank of the Suippes to Aubérive and west from Aubérive to Mont Sans Nom, 2.4 km (1.5 mi) south-east of Le Téton. The 24th Division with 4+1⁄2 battalions, attacked on a line from the salient at Bois des Abatis, west to the Suippes, north of Bois des Sapins.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: German counter-attacks in the XII _____ area on 19, 20 and 22 April, recaptured some lost ground
Battle of the Hills.fact: In the XII Corps area on the right flank, the 24th Division, Moroccan Division and the 75th Territorial Regiment of XVII Corps, were to attack from the east bank of the Suippes to Aubérive and west from Aubérive to Mont Sans Nom, 2.4 km (1.5 mi) south-east of Le Téton. German counter-attacks in the XII Corps area on 19, 20 and 22 April, recaptured some lost ground.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The RMLE advanced through a downpour to _____ and then overran Le Golfe; early on 18 April, Byzance, Dardanelles and Prince Eitel trenches, to the south-west of Aubérive were captured
Battle of the Hills.fact: The RMLE advanced through a downpour to Bouleaux Trench and then overran Le Golfe; early on 18 April, Byzance, Dardanelles and Prince Eitel trenches, to the south-west of Aubérive were captured.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: To the west, the _____ counter-barrage was fired late and Mont Sans Nom was captured by 5:00 a.m
Battle of the Hills.fact: The attack achieved a measure of surprise but the German defence on the left flank, held up the French advance at Levant Trench and in Bois Allonge, which were eventually captured, before the advance resumed on Landsturm Trench. To the west, the German counter-barrage was fired late and Mont Sans Nom was captured by 5:00 a.m.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: In the XVII Corps area, the 33rd _____ attacked with the 11th Regiment on the right towards Le Téton and the 20th Regiment against Le Casque
Battle of the Hills.fact: In the XVII Corps area, the 33rd Division attacked with the 11th Regiment on the right towards Le Téton and the 20th Regiment against Le Casque.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The 11th _____ advance began at 4:45 a.m., accompanied by a battery of light field guns
Battle of the Hills.fact: In the XVII Corps area, the 33rd Division attacked with the 11th Regiment on the right towards Le Téton and the 20th Regiment against Le Casque. The 11th Regiment advance began at 4:45 a.m., accompanied by a battery of light field guns.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The 20th _____ captured redoubts around Bois du Chien, after fighting all day and then began preparing a dawn attack Le Casque
Battle of the Hills.fact: In the XVII Corps area, the 33rd Division attacked with the 11th Regiment on the right towards Le Téton and the 20th Regiment against Le Casque. The 11th Regiment advance began at 4:45 a.m., accompanied by a battery of light field guns.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The advance had begun while the _____ front-line infantry was still sheltering underground and the German artillery did not begin barrage-fire until 5:05 a.m
Battle of the Hills.fact: The advance had begun while the German front-line infantry was still sheltering underground and the German artillery did not begin barrage-fire until 5:05 a.m. The advance towards Bois-en-Escalier in the centre began well and several field-gun batteries stood by to follow the advance, after a short delay at the German first line in Bois-en-Escalier, where the Germans were outflanked from the north and killed or captured.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Erfurt Trench was overrun and then the _____ was attacked from the west
Battle of the Hills.fact: The capture of the Konstanzlager was vital to the possession of Mont Blond and the final objectives along the twin summits of Mont Haut, the north-west trench of Le Casque and Mont Perthois to the south, between Mont Haut and Le Casque. Erfurt Trench was overrun and then the Konstanzlager was attacked from the west.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Later in the day, reserves from the 34th _____ were sent forward and when part of Erfurt Trench fell, the Konstanzlager was attacked from the east
Battle of the Hills.fact: Later in the day, reserves from the 34th Division were sent forward and when part of Erfurt Trench fell, the Konstanzlager was attacked from the east.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: By 6.45 a.m., part of _____ and the communication trenches leading towards it, had been captured but the Germans retained a foothold, at the west end of the trench
Battle of the Hills.fact: At 5:45 a.m., the French took the east end of Erfurt Trench, despite delays as some redoubts held out, reached the edge of Bois de Mont Perthois by noon and then repulsed four German counter-attacks before nightfall. By 6.45 a.m., part of Erfurt Trench and the communication trenches leading towards it, had been captured but the Germans retained a foothold, at the west end of the trench.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The troops on the left were exposed by the repulse of the troops to the west, beyond the _____–Nauroy road
Battle of the Hills.fact: In the VIII Corps area, the 34th Division east of the Thuizy–Nauroy road, attacked at 4.45 a.m., with two regiments and an hour later, could be seen threading their way up the heights, bombing dug-outs and fighting hand-to-hand in the open with German infantry. The troops on the left were exposed by the repulse of the troops to the west, beyond the Thuizy–Nauroy road.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: German resistance in the _____ to the south-east of Mont Blond, prevented its right from being supported by the 45th division
Battle of the Hills.fact: German resistance in the Konstanzlager to the south-east of Mont Blond, prevented its right from being supported by the 45th division. The Germans in the west end of Erfurt Trench repulsed the attack and the left flank regiment of the 45th Division to the right, was held up at the Konstanzlager.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The 83rd _____ managed a costly advance to the summit of Mont Cornillet but German machine-guns on the ridge between Mont Cornillet and Mont Blond, slowed the advance
Battle of the Hills.fact: The 83rd Regiment resumed the advance on Mont Cornillet and the 59th Regiment attacked Mont Blond the 34th Division took nearly all of its objectives on Mont Cornillet and Mont Blond, at the west end of the Moronvilliers massif. The 83rd Regiment managed a costly advance to the summit of Mont Cornillet but German machine-guns on the ridge between Mont Cornillet and Mont Blond, slowed the advance.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The left flank of the 59th _____ was stopped by the Germans at Flensburg Trench, which connected the German defences of Mont Cornillet and Mont Blond, losing touch with the 83rd Regiment
Battle of the Hills.fact: The 83rd Regiment managed a costly advance to the summit of Mont Cornillet but German machine-guns on the ridge between Mont Cornillet and Mont Blond, slowed the advance. The left flank of the 59th Regiment was stopped by the Germans at Flensburg Trench, which connected the German defences of Mont Cornillet and Mont Blond, losing touch with the 83rd Regiment.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The Germans in the west end of _____ repulsed the attack and the left flank regiment of the 45th Division to the right, was held up at the Konstanzlager
Battle of the Hills.fact: The Germans in the west end of Erfurt Trench repulsed the attack and the left flank regiment of the 45th Division to the right, was held up at the Konstanzlager. Lobit, the 34th division commander, sent the reserve battalions of the two regiments, to guard the open western flank of the division, between Erfurt trench and Mont Cornillet and to close the gap between the 83rd and 59th regiments.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Some companies were sent to outflank the _____ from the west
Battle of the Hills.fact: The Germans in the west end of Erfurt Trench repulsed the attack and the left flank regiment of the 45th Division to the right, was held up at the Konstanzlager. Some companies were sent to outflank the Konstanzlager from the west.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: At 2:30 p.m., the _____ garrison and reinforcements from the tunnel under the hill, broke into the French position on Mont Cornillet
Battle of the Hills.fact: Field artillery from the 128th Division was galloped up the slopes of Mont Cornillet, despite German return fire and the 34th Division was subjected to a heavy German bombardment and counter-attacks against both flanks. At 2:30 p.m., the German garrison and reinforcements from the tunnel under the hill, broke into the French position on Mont Cornillet.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: More _____ attacks were made at nightfall but French field and heavy artillery fire, repulsed the German infantry, except for a short time on the left flank
Battle of the Hills.fact: At 2:30 p.m., the German garrison and reinforcements from the tunnel under the hill, broke into the French position on Mont Cornillet. The 2nd Battalion of the 83rd Regiment, held on to the north end of the trench until 5:30 p.m., when it ran out of ammunition and withdrew behind the crest, where the survivors repulsed a German attack at midnight.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The 16th Division (_____), attacked on the extreme left flank, west of the Thuizy–Nauroy road against Bois de la Grille and Leopoldshöhe Trench
Battle of the Hills.fact: The 16th Division (General Le Gallais), attacked on the extreme left flank, west of the Thuizy–Nauroy road against Bois de la Grille and Leopoldshöhe Trench.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: Having gained its objectives, the division was to face west and north, to guard the rear of the 34th _____ to the east, as it attacked Mont Cornillet and Mont Blond
Battle of the Hills.fact: The 16th Division (General Le Gallais), attacked on the extreme left flank, west of the Thuizy–Nauroy road against Bois de la Grille and Leopoldshöhe Trench. Having gained its objectives, the division was to face west and north, to guard the rear of the 34th Division to the east, as it attacked Mont Cornillet and Mont Blond.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The objectives of the 16th Division were on a slight incline, which in the conditions of _____, was more dangerous to the attacking force than a steep one, because of the lack of dead ground
Battle of the Hills.fact: The objectives of the 16th Division were on a slight incline, which in the conditions of 1917, was more dangerous to the attacking force than a steep one, because of the lack of dead ground.

Battle of the Hills.subject: International Relations
Battle of the Hills.question: The two regiments in the centre and on the right were stopped by the German machine-gun fire from _____, which ran from the Thuizy–Nauroy road, through the south end of Bois de la Grille
